title: Renyi's theorem, Renyi 1948: every large even number is a prime plus a number with at most 8 prime factors
abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof of Renyi's theorem: there is N0 such that every even N >= N0 is p + m with p prime, m >= 1 and Omega of m at most 8, where Omega counts prime factors with multiplicity, as Mathlib's ArithmeticFunction.cardFactors does. So the theorem is proved with the explicit constant K = 8. Also proved: a lower bound e^{-36} N / 2 log^2 N for the number of primes p < N with Omega of N - p at most 8; the same two statements with the weaker K = 13000; and the K = 8 statement written with Mathlib's Nat.IsAtMostAlmostPrime. The entry also proves twin_renyi_count, a derived analogue proved in this entry by the same sieve method, a twin-prime analogue of Renyi's theorem, not a result of Renyi 1948. The proof is a Brun type block sieve with Bonferroni levels whose remainders are bounded by the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem proved in the same library; all thresholds are ineffective through Siegel's theorem. Nothing here is new mathematics: Pan has K = 4 and Chen 1973 has K = 2. Binary Goldbach is Omega of m equal to 1; it is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent; the statements were checked against the literature by AI reviewers and are offered for human audit.
